---
name: tempo-timesheet
description: Use when the user asks about their Tempo timesheet — summarizing logged work for a day or week, checking what was logged on a Jira issue, finding duplicates, or creating/updating Tempo worklogs. Enforces the preview-then-approve workflow and never writes without explicit approval.
---

# Tempo Timesheet Operations

You have access to a Tempo Timesheets MCP server with 9 tools backed by the
Tempo v4 REST API and (when configured) the Jira Cloud v3 API.

## Tools

| Tool                     | Purpose                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tempo_get_worklogs`     | List recorded worklogs in a date range (scoped to the caller's account by default) |
| `tempo_get_worklog`      | Fetch one worklog by id                                                            |
| `tempo_get_week_summary` | Aggregate one week (Mon–Sun) by day and issue                                      |
| `jira_search_issues`     | Search Jira issues via JQL (helps resolve issue keys)                              |
| `tempo_preview_worklog`  | Dry-run a create: validates, checks duplicates, returns an approval token          |
| `tempo_validate_worklog` | Validate a proposal without issuing an approval token                              |
| `tempo_check_duplicate`  | Check a proposal against existing worklogs for that issue/date                     |
| `tempo_create_worklog`   | Create a worklog (requires approval token + `confirm: true`)                       |
| `tempo_update_worklog`   | Update an existing worklog (requires approval token + `confirm: true`)             |

## Hard rules

1. **Never call `tempo_create_worklog` or `tempo_update_worklog` without a
   fresh preview.** The approval token is bound to the exact payload (by
   numeric issueId) — if the user changes anything (issue, date, duration,
   description), you MUST run `tempo_preview_worklog` again to get a new
   token. Reusing a token after any change fails by design.
2. **Pass `confirm: true` only after the user has approved the preview.** Show
   the preview (issue, date, duration, duplicates) and ask. Do not treat
   silence as approval.
3. **A validation success is not an approval.** Even if `tempo_validate_worklog`
   returns no errors, the write path still needs a preview + token + confirm.
4. **Never retry an uncertain write.** If a create/update returns
   `UNCERTAIN_OUTCOME`, the result is unknown. Check with `tempo_get_worklogs`
   for the affected date and report to the user before doing anything else.
   A clean (non-uncertain) failure keeps the token valid: the user may retry
   deliberately with the SAME payload without a new preview.
5. **Never delete worklogs.** The server has no delete tool by design.
6. **Read tools are scoped to the caller's account by default.** Pass an
   explicit `authorAccountId` only when the user asks to inspect another
   user's logs; when the tool response reports unfiltered results
   (`authorScope: null`), say so — totals may include other users' worklogs.

## Summaries use recorded data only

`tempo_get_week_summary` reports RECORDED worklogs only. Days with no records
may be days off, holidays, or unlogged work — the server cannot tell. When the
user asks "did I log everything this week?", present the per-day totals and
explicitly list the days without records; never invent gaps or assume missed
work.

## Typical flows

**Daily summary:** call `tempo_get_worklogs` for the date (or
`tempo_get_week_summary` for a week), group by issue, report totals plus days
without records.

**Log new work:**

1. `tempo_preview_worklog` with issueKey, date, durationMinutes, description.
2. Show the user: resolved issue, computed seconds, duplicates found, warnings.
3. If duplicates exist (especially `high` confidence), ask whether to proceed.
4. On explicit approval, call `tempo_create_worklog` with the SAME values plus
   the `approvalToken` and `confirm: true`.
5. Report the created worklog id and whether post-write verification succeeded.

**Update existing work:** call `tempo_preview_worklog` with `operation: "update"`,
`worklogId`, and `changes`. Show the before/after to the user and follow the
same approval ritual, then call `tempo_update_worklog` with the same worklogId,
changes, token, and `confirm: true`.

# Tempo Timesheet MCP Server

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/s-tempo-worklog-mcp)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/s-tempo-worklog-mcp)
[![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A520-blue)](https://nodejs.org)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/s-tempo-worklog-mcp)](LICENSE)

A local MCP server (stdio) that gives coding agents such as OpenCode or Claude
Code safe, read-first access to **Tempo Timesheets** (REST API v4) and
**Jira Cloud** (REST API v3): summarize logged work, detect duplicates, and —
only through an explicit preview → approval → write pipeline — create or
update worklogs.

> Read-only by default. Writes are triple-gated: `WORKLOG_WRITE_ENABLED=true`
> **and** a single-use payload-bound approval token **and** `confirm: true`.
> There is no delete tool.

## How it works

```
┌─────────────────────┐   MCP over stdio    ┌──────────────────────┐   REST API v4   ┌────────────────────┐
│   Coding agent      │◄───────────────────►│  s-tempo-worklog-mcp │ ───────────────►│  Tempo Timesheets  │
│  (OpenCode, Claude  │    9 tools (JSON)   │  (this MCP server)   │                 │      (v4)          │
│  Code, any client)  │                     │  validate · approve  │ ───────────────►├────────────────────┤
└─────────────────────┘                     │  write               │   REST API v3   │      Jira Cloud    │
        ▲                                   └──────────┬───────────┘                 │      (v3)          │
        │  /tempo-today  /tempo-week  /tempo-log       │                             └────────────────────┘
        │  (OpenCode slash commands)                   │  all credentials stay local
        └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘  (env vars / .env)
```

- **You** (or your agent) issue commands in the CLI — natural language or the
  bundled slash commands.
- The **agent** calls this MCP server over stdio; the server owns validation,
  duplicate detection, and the approval pipeline.
- The server talks **only** to the Tempo v4 and (optionally) Jira v3 REST APIs.
  Credentials never leave your machine; the server is stdio-only.

### The write pipeline (triple-gated)

```
 preview ──► user approval ──► write (confirm + single-use token) ──► verify
```

1. `tempo_preview_worklog` validates the proposal, runs duplicate detection,
   and issues an approval token bound to the SHA-256 of the payload.
2. You review and approve. Any change to the payload invalidates the token.
3. The write tool requires `WORKLOG_WRITE_ENABLED=true`, the token, and an
   explicit `confirm: true`. Tokens are **single-use** — a replayed approval
   cannot create a second identical worklog. Timed-out writes return
   `UNCERTAIN_OUTCOME` and are never retried by the server.

## Tools (9)

| Tool                     | Kind          | Description                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tempo_get_worklogs`     | read          | Worklogs in a date range; scoped to your own account by default                     |
| `tempo_get_worklog`      | read          | One worklog by id                                                                   |
| `tempo_get_week_summary` | read          | Week (Mon–Sun) aggregated by day and issue                                          |
| `jira_search_issues`     | read          | Jira search via JQL (enhanced search API)                                           |
| `tempo_preview_worklog`  | preview       | Validate + duplicate-check a create/update; returns an approval token. Never writes |
| `tempo_validate_worklog` | preview       | Validate a proposal without issuing a token                                         |
| `tempo_check_duplicate`  | preview       | Confidence-scored duplicate check for a candidate entry                             |
| `tempo_create_worklog`   | write (gated) | Create a worklog; needs token + `confirm`                                           |
| `tempo_update_worklog`   | write (gated) | Update a worklog; needs token + `confirm`                                           |

The write flow is: **preview → show the user → explicit approval → write with
the same exact payload**. The approval token is bound to the SHA-256 of the
payload (identified by numeric `issueId`), expires in 15 minutes, is consumed
by a successful write, and is invalidated by any change. Writes that time out
return `UNCERTAIN_OUTCOME` and are never retried by the server.

## Install

**Run directly with npx (no installation):**

```bash
npx -y s-tempo-worklog-mcp
```

**Or install globally:**

```bash
npm install -g s-tempo-worklog-mcp
tempo-worklog-mcp
```

The server reads configuration from environment variables. Create a `.env`
file next to where you run it, or set them in your MCP client config.

| Variable                | Default                | Description                                                              |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `TEMPO_API_TOKEN`       | — (required)           | Tempo API token                                                          |
| `TEMPO_ACCOUNT_ID`      | auto-detected          | Your Tempo accountId; auto-detected from an existing worklog when absent |
| `TEMPO_BASE_URL`        | `https://api.tempo.io` | Tempo v4 base URL                                                        |
| `JIRA_BASE_URL`         | — (optional)           | `https://<site>.atlassian.net`                                           |
| `JIRA_EMAIL`            | — (optional)           | Atlassian account email                                                  |
| `JIRA_API_TOKEN`        | — (optional)           | Atlassian API token                                                      |
| `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE`      | system TZ              | IANA name, e.g. `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`                                       |
| `LOG_LEVEL`             | `info`                 | `debug` \| `info` \| `warn` \| `error`                                   |
| `WORKLOG_WRITE_ENABLED` | `false`                | Master switch for write tools                                            |

Jira is optional but recommended: Tempo v4 returns only numeric issue ids, so
without Jira the tools cannot display issue keys. All three `JIRA_*` variables
must be set together. See `.env.example` for a ready-made template.

## Quick start (from source)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nbhson/tool-logwork-mcp
cd tool-logwork-mcp
npm install
npm run build
cp .env.example .env   # then fill in TEMPO_API_TOKEN (+ Jira if desired)
node dist/index.js
```

Full setup for OpenCode (MCP registration, skill, commands, troubleshooting):
[docs/setup-opencode.md](docs/setup-opencode.md).

## Registering with MCP clients

The server speaks MCP over stdio. Generic pattern — run
`npx -y s-tempo-worklog-mcp` as the command and pass environment variables:

**OpenCode** (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` or project `opencode.json`):

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "tempo-worklog": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "s-tempo-worklog-mcp"],
      "environment": {
        "TEMPO_API_TOKEN": "your-tempo-token",
        "JIRA_BASE_URL": "https://your-site.atlassian.net",
        "JIRA_EMAIL": "you@example.com",
        "JIRA_API_TOKEN": "your-jira-token"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Claude Code:**

```bash
claude mcp add tempo-worklog \
  -e TEMPO_API_TOKEN=your-tempo-token \
  -- npx -y s-tempo-worklog-mcp
```

## OpenCode skill & slash commands

This repository ships an agent skill and four slash commands (`.opencode/`).
After installing from npm, copy them into your project:

```bash
# OpenCode loads skills/commands from your project's .opencode/ directory
mkdir -p .opencode/skills
cp -r node_modules/s-tempo-worklog-mcp/.opencode/skills/tempo-timesheet .opencode/skills/
cp -r node_modules/s-tempo-worklog-mcp/.opencode/commands ./
```

This gives you:

- `.opencode/skills/tempo-timesheet/SKILL.md` — tool catalog + hard rules
  (preview-before-write, never retry uncertain writes, recorded-data-only
  summaries).
- `.opencode/commands/tempo-today.md` — `/tempo-today` daily summary with an
  aligned terminal report.
- `.opencode/commands/tempo-week.md` — `/tempo-week` weekly timesheet with
  per-day and per-issue breakdowns.
- `.opencode/commands/tempo-log.md` — `/tempo-log ABC-123 2h30m ...` with the
  preview card and approval ritual baked in. Accepts a single entry or a
  batch of entries, inline or pasted from txt/md/csv/freeform text.
- `.opencode/commands/tempo-log-rewrite.md` — `/tempo-log-rewrite` works like
  `/tempo-log` but first rewrites each description into a professional,
  concise work-log entry while strictly preserving its meaning. Both the
  original and the rewritten description are shown in the preview for
  verification; approval and the write pipeline are unchanged.

Details: [docs/setup-opencode.md](docs/setup-opencode.md).

## Safety model

- **Read-first.** Every read tool is safe to call; nothing writes unless you
  go through the pipeline.
- **Triple-gated writes.** `WORKLOG_WRITE_ENABLED=true` + preview approval
  token + `confirm: true`. The token binds to the SHA-256 of the exact payload
  (identified by numeric `issueId`, so a Jira hiccup between preview and write
  cannot invalidate a valid approval), expires in 15 minutes, and is consumed
  on success — no replay, no duplicates from retries.
- **Uncertain outcomes are reported, never retried.** A timed-out write
  returns `UNCERTAIN_OUTCOME`; the server never auto-retries a write.
- **Honest scoping.** Read tools scope results to your own account by default
  and say so; totals never silently mix in other users' worklogs.
- **No delete.** Tempo delete is intentionally not exposed.
- **Recorded data only.** Summaries count recorded worklogs only — no invented
  hours, no assumed work.

## Troubleshooting

Every tool error envelope carries a stable machine-readable `code` and, for
common operational failures, an actionable `hint` field. The most common ones:

| Error code                  | Meaning & what to do                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AUTH_ERROR` (401)          | Token missing/expired/revoked. Generate a fresh token (Tempo: Settings → API Integration; Jira: id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens), update the env var, restart the server. |
| `PERMISSION_ERROR` (403)    | Token valid but lacks scope/visibility (Tempo needs the Worklogs scope; check Jira project access).                                                                                |
| `WRITE_DISABLED`            | Writes are off by default. Set `WORKLOG_WRITE_ENABLED=true` and restart, then **re-run the preview** for a fresh token.                                                            |
| `APPROVAL_REQUIRED`         | Token expired (>15 min), consumed, or the payload changed. Call `tempo_preview_worklog` again.                                                                                     |
| `UNCERTAIN_OUTCOME`         | The write MAY have landed. Verify with `tempo_get_worklog(s)` before any retry — never blind-retry.                                                                                |
| `NETWORK_ERROR` / `TIMEOUT` | Check connectivity/VPN/proxy (`HTTPS_PROXY`). For a timed-out write, verify before retrying.                                                                                       |
| `CONFIG_ERROR`              | Configuration incomplete — compare with `.env.example` and restart.                                                                                                                |
| `RATE_LIMIT` (429)          | Wait for the suggested interval, then retry; narrow the date range or lower `maxResults`.                                                                                          |

More environment-specific symptoms (Jira partial config, auto-detection on a
fresh account, timezone off-by-one): [docs/setup-opencode.md](docs/setup-opencode.md).

## Development

```bash
npm run typecheck        # strict typecheck of src
npm run typecheck:test   # typecheck of src + tests
npm run lint             # eslint (src + tests)
npm run format           # prettier
npm test                 # vitest (unit + integration, mocked HTTP)
npm run build            # tsc -> dist/
npm start                # run the stdio server
```

Test suite: **143 tests, all passing** (unit: config, context helpers, date —
including timezone/week-boundary cases, duration, logger/error hints, approval,
report, duplicate, TTL cache; integration: Tempo client, Jira client, worklog
service, weekly-summary timezone regression (UTC/+7/+9/+10/−10, Sunday vs
Monday week anchoring, mocked clock), and the full MCP tool handler surface;
protocol-level: a real MCP `Client` over an `InMemoryTransport` pair exercises
initialize, `tools/list` (all 9 tools + JSON Schemas), and tool-call envelopes
end-to-end). HTTP is fully mocked — no credentials or network needed.
Coverage (v8): ~89% statements, ~78% branches, ~92% lines
(`npm run test:coverage`). `npm publish` runs the full gate automatically via
`prepublishOnly`.

as built.

## Known limitations

- **No delete.** Tempo delete is intentionally not exposed in this MVP.
- **Update identifier risk.** Tempo docs disagree on `issueKey` vs `issueId`
  for `PUT /worklogs/{id}`; this server sends `issueId`
  ([docs/api-contract.md](docs/api-contract.md)).
- **Single user focus.** Read tools default to your own account (pass
  `authorAccountId` to inspect another user); admin-style logging for others
  is out of scope.
- **Approval state is in memory.** Restarting the server invalidates pending
  approval tokens (by design — re-preview is cheap and safe).
- **No Overtime/Capacity/accounts endpoints.** Worklogs and issue search only.
- **Caller identity needs one worklog.** Auto-detecting your account reads the
  author of your most recent worklog; on a brand-new account with zero
  worklogs, set `TEMPO_ACCOUNT_ID` explicitly.

## What's new in 0.4.0

- **Fixed** auto-detection of the Tempo account id (it previously read the
  wrong endpoint and could send a wrong `authorAccountId` on create).
- **Read tools now scope to your own account by default**, so totals never
  silently include other users' worklogs; pass `authorAccountId` to override.
- **Approval tokens are single-use** — no replay/duplicate window after a
  successful write (still reusable when a write fails cleanly).
- Approvals are bound by numeric `issueId`, so a Jira hiccup between preview
  and write no longer invalidates a valid approval.
- Updating a worklog no longer fails when its existing duration is not a
  whole number of minutes (e.g. timer-derived `89m30s`).
- Pagination: results are never returned beyond `maxResults`, and exhausted
  pagination now fails loudly instead of silently truncating.
- Cleaner validation errors for malformed create previews (no crash on
  missing description); `tempo_update_worklog` now returns the structured
  `WRITE_DISABLED` error code like `tempo_create_worklog`.

## What's new in 0.6.0

- **Multi-log support.** `tempo_preview_worklog`, `tempo_create_worklog`, and
  `tempo_validate_worklog` now accept either a single entry (as before) or a
  batch of entries via `proposals` / `entries` / `items` / `worklogs` / `logs` /
  `batch`. A batch preview issues a single approval token bound to the whole
  batch; the write runs entries sequentially and reports per-entry results
  (created / failed / uncertain) without blind-retrying uncertain writes.

---
description: Log Tempo work for one or MANY issues with AI-rewritten professional descriptions (preview first, write only after approval)
---

Log Tempo work for Jira issue(s), rewriting long/rough descriptions into
professional ones. Accepts a single entry or a BATCH of entries, given inline
or as pasted/attached content (txt, md, csv, table, bullet list, freeform
prompt text).

## Input — how to parse `$ARGUMENTS`

`$ARGUMENTS` may be, in any of these forms:

1. **Single inline entry**: `issueKey date duration description`
   (e.g. `ABC-123 2026-10-28 2h30m Fixed the login bug`).
2. **Multiple inline entries**: several entries in one message, separated by
   newlines, blank lines, bullets, or numbering.
3. **A file path or pasted content** (`.txt`, `.md`, `.csv`, or raw prompt):
   read/inspect it and extract every loggable entry. Supported shapes:
   - CSV rows / markdown tables with columns like issue, date, duration/hours,
     description (column order and header naming may vary — infer them);
   - bullet or numbered lists mentioning an issue key + time + what was done;
   - freeform prose mentioning several tickets ("spend 2h on ABC-123 fixing
     ... then 1h on ABC-456 ...").
4. **Mixed**: a file plus extra inline notes that override or add entries.

Parsing rules:

- Each entry resolves to: issueKey, date, duration, description.
- A date stated once at the top (or in the prompt) applies to entries without
  their own date; default to today.
- Accept durations as `1h30m`, `90m`, `1.5h`, `2`, `2.0` (decimal hours) —
  infer from context; a bare number next to "hours"/"h" is decimal hours.
- Never guess an issue key. Entries without a resolvable issue key are listed
  as SKIPPED with the reason, not silently dropped.
- If nothing at all is parseable, ask for the missing parts instead of
  inventing entries.

## Per-entry pipeline

For EACH parsed entry, in order:

1. **Rewrite the description** before anything else. Rules for the rewrite:
   - **Meaning is sacred**: keep every fact the user stated (what was done,
     on which component/feature, outcomes, follow-ups). Never invent details,
     ticket numbers, metrics, or work that was not mentioned.
   - Make it professional and concise: clear sentence(s), no filler words, no
     greetings, no first-person chatter.
   - Prefer work-log phrasing: start with the action verb in past tense
     ("Implemented", "Fixed", "Investigated", "Refactored").
   - Keep domain terms, issue-specific names, and technical keywords exactly
     as given (they matter for searchability).
   - Preserve the original language of the description (Vietnamese stays
     Vietnamese, English stays English); do not translate.
   - If a description contains multiple distinct pieces of work, keep them as
     short separated clauses or semicolons — do not drop any.
   - Target length: 1–3 sentences, roughly ≤ 200 characters when possible.
     Only go longer if dropping text would lose meaning.

2. Call `tempo_preview_worklog` for that entry with the REWRITTEN description:
   `{ operation: "create", issueKey, date, durationMinutes, description }`.
   Each entry gets its own `approvalToken` — tokens are never shared.

3. Present ONE combined preview card listing every entry, EXACTLY:

   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────
   │ 👁 PREVIEW — create 3 worklogs (rewritten)
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

   1. Issue ABC-123 — Fix login bug (In Progress)
      Date 2026-10-30 · Duration 2h 30m (9000s)
      Description (original)
      "fixed the login bug, it was a null check issue and added some tests too"
      Description (rewritten)
      "Fixed login bug caused by missing null check; added unit tests"

   2. Issue ABC-456 — Review PR
      Date 2026-10-30 · Duration 1h 00m (3600s)
      ...

   ⚠ Duplicates: entry 2 duplicates worklog #9988 (same issue/date/duration)
   ⚠ Skipped: 1 line had no issue key ("half day meetings stuff")
   ⚠ Warnings: date is in the future

   ─────────────────────────────────────────────
   Approve all? [y/N] (or approve selectively, e.g. "1 only")

   - ALWAYS show both the original and the rewritten description for EVERY
     entry so the user can verify meaning was preserved;
   - if any rewrite changed or dropped something the user might care about,
     point it out explicitly below the card;
   - ALSO flag cross-entry duplicates WITHIN the batch: two entries logging
     the same issue + date;
   - show duplicates and warnings prominently; a `high`-confidence duplicate
     must be called out and re-confirmed explicitly;
   - show the computed `timeSpentSeconds` for each entry.

4. Ask for explicit approval. Do NOT proceed on silence. Approval may be for
   all entries or a selected subset ("only 1 and 3" → log only those). If the
   user rejects or edits any rewrite, apply their wording and re-run the
   preview for the affected entries only (a changed payload always needs a
   new preview).

5. Only for approved entries, call `tempo_create_worklog` sequentially — each
   with its OWN rewritten values, its OWN `approvalToken`, and
   `confirm: true`. Never batch two creates into one call.

6. Report per entry:

   ✅ Created worklog #12345 for ABC-123 on 2026-10-30 (2h 30m)
   ✅ Created worklog #12346 for ABC-456 on 2026-10-30 (1h 00m)
   ✔ Verified against the Tempo API after the writes.

   If any write returns `UNCERTAIN_OUTCOME` for that entry:
   ⚠ Outcome unknown for ABC-456 — do NOT retry it. Checking
   `tempo_get_worklogs` for the date... — then run that check and report.

description: Log Tempo work for one or MANY Jira issues (preview first, write only after approval)
---

Log Tempo work for Jira issue(s). Accepts a single entry or a BATCH of entries,
given inline or as pasted/attached content (txt, md, csv, table, bullet list,
freeform prompt text).

## Input — how to parse `$ARGUMENTS`

`$ARGUMENTS` may be, in any of these forms:

1. **Single inline entry**: `issueKey date duration description`
   (e.g. `ABC-123 2026-10-28 2h30m Fixed the login bug`).
2. **Multiple inline entries**: several entries in one message, separated by
   newlines, blank lines, bullets, or numbering.
3. **A file path or pasted content** (`.txt`, `.md`, `.csv`, or raw prompt):
   read/inspect it and extract every loggable entry. Supported shapes:
   - CSV rows / markdown tables with columns like issue, date, duration/hours,
     description (column order and header naming may vary — infer them);
   - bullet or numbered lists mentioning an issue key + time + what was done;
   - freeform prose mentioning several tickets ("spend 2h on ABC-123 fixing
     ... then 1h on ABC-456 ...").
4. **Mixed**: a file plus extra inline notes that override or add entries.

Parsing rules:

- Each entry resolves to: issueKey, date, duration, description.
- A date stated once at the top (or in the prompt) applies to entries without
  their own date; default to today.
- Accept durations as `1h30m`, `90m`, `1.5h`, `2`, `2.0` (decimal hours) —
  infer from context; a bare number next to "hours"/"h" is decimal hours.
- Never guess an issue key. Entries without a resolvable issue key are listed
  as SKIPPED with the reason, not silently dropped.
- If nothing at all is parseable, ask for the missing parts instead of
  inventing entries.

## Per-entry pipeline

For EACH parsed entry, in order:

1. Call `tempo_preview_worklog` with flattened create args:
   `{ operation: "create", issueKey, date, durationMinutes, description }`.
   Each entry gets its own `approvalToken` — tokens are never shared.

2. Present ONE combined preview card listing every entry, EXACTLY:

   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────

   2. Issue ABC-456 — Review PR

      ...

   ⚠ Duplicates: entry 2 duplicates worklog #9988 (same issue/date/duration)
   ⚠ Skipped: 1 line had no issue key ("half day meetings stuff")
   ⚠ Warnings: date is in the future

   ─────────────────────────────────────────────
   Approve all? [y/N] (or approve selectively, e.g. "1 only")

   - show duplicates and warnings prominently; a `high`-confidence duplicate
     must be called out and re-confirmed explicitly;
   - ALSO flag cross-entry duplicates WITHIN the batch: two entries logging
     the same issue + date;
   - show the computed `timeSpentSeconds` so the user sees the exact payload.

3. Ask for explicit approval. Do NOT proceed on silence. Approval may be for
   all entries or a selected subset ("only 1 and 3" → log only those). A
   changed payload always needs a new preview.

4. Only for approved entries, call `tempo_create_worklog` sequentially — each
   with its OWN values, its OWN `approvalToken`, and `confirm: true`. Never
   batch two creates into one call.

5. Report per entry:

   ✅ Created worklog #12345 for ABC-123 on 2026-10-30 (2h 30m)
   ✅ Created worklog #12346 for ABC-456 on 2026-10-30 (1h 00m)
   ✔ Verified against the Tempo API after the writes.

description: Summarize today's logged Tempo work
---

Summarize my Tempo worklog for today (`$ARGUMENTS` overrides the date; a date in
YYYY-MM-DD is also accepted).

1. Determine the target date: use `$ARGUMENTS` if provided, otherwise today in
   the configured timezone.
2. Call `tempo_get_worklogs` for that single date.
3. Render the result using EXACTLY this layout (plain text, no extra prose):

   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────
   │ ⏱ TEMPO — Thứ Hai, 2026-10-30
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

   ▸ ABC-123 Fix login bug .............. 2h 30m
   "Implemented auth flow and unit tests"
   ▸ ABC-456 Review PR .................. 1h 00m

   ─────────────────────────────────────────────
   ✔ Total: 3h 30m across 2 issues

   Rules for the report:
   - one `▸` line per issue: `<key>  <summary/title>  <time>`;
   - align the time column; use `....` leaders where it improves readability;
   - end with a `───` divider and a `Total` line;
   - if Jira is unavailable and a key shows as `issue-{id}`, display the raw id
     and note that Jira was not reachable for key resolution.

4. If nothing was logged, output the header, then:
   `✖ No worklogs recorded on <date>.` and offer to log work via
   `tempo_preview_worklog`.

Use recorded worklogs only. Do not speculate about unlogged time unless the
user asks; if you mention gaps, be explicit that these are hours without
records.

description: Summarize this week's Tempo timesheet

2. Call `tempo_get_week_summary` for that week.
